description: A comprehensive study of the behavior of solid structures subjected to various loads, focusing on determinacy, internal forces, deflection analysis, and advanced matrix methods.

sections.title: Static and Kinematic Indeterminacy
sections.description: Evaluating the structural stability and identifying the number of unknown forces or displacements required to analyze a structure.

equations: Rigid Jointed Plane Frame: Ds = (3 * m + r) - 3 * j
Pin Jointed Plane Frame (Truss): Ds = (m + r) - 2 * j

formulas.category: Kinematic Indeterminacy (Dk) or Degrees of Freedom
equations: Rigid Jointed Plane Frame: Dk = 3 * j - re
Pin Jointed Plane Frame: Dk = 2 * j - re
Note: Subtract the number of inextensible members from Dk if axial deformation is neglected.

sections.title: Shear Force and Bending Moment
sections.description: Understanding internal resisting forces and moments developed in structural members under transverse loading.

key_concepts.explanation: The rate of change of shear force equals the negative of the load intensity (dV/dx = -w). The rate of change of bending moment equals the shear force (dM/dx = V). Maximum bending moment occurs where shear force is zero or changes sign.
The specific point on a bending moment diagram where the bending moment changes sign (transitions from positive/sagging to negative/hogging, or vice versa).

cases.condition: Simply Supported Beam with a Uniformly Distributed Load (UDL) of 'w' over span 'L'
results: Bending Moment Diagram shape is a Parabola (2nd degree curve)

sections.title: Deflection of Beams
sections.description: Methods and standard formulas for calculating the maximum slope and deflection in flexural members.

steps.title: Moment Area Method - Theorem I
steps.detail: The change in slope between any two points on the elastic curve equals the area of the M/EI diagram between those two points.

steps.title: Moment Area Method - Theorem II
steps.detail: The vertical deviation of the tangent at point A with respect to the tangent at point B equals the moment of the M/EI diagram area between A and B, taken about point A.

steps.title: Conjugate Beam Method
steps.detail: An imaginary beam with the same length as the real beam, loaded with the M/EI diagram. The shear force in the conjugate beam gives the slope in the real beam, and the bending moment gives the deflection.

cases.condition: Cantilever Beam of length 'L' with a Point Load 'P' at the free end
results: Maximum Slope (at free end) = (P * L^2) / (2 * E * I)
Maximum Deflection (at free end) = (P * L^3) / (3 * E * I)

cases.condition: Simply Supported Beam of length 'L' with a central Point Load 'P'
results: Maximum Slope (at supports) = (P * L^2) / (16 * E * I)
Maximum Deflection (at center) = (P * L^3) / (48 * E * I)

sections.title: Influence Line Diagrams (ILD)
sections.description: Graphical representations showing the variation of a reaction, shear, moment, or deflection at a specific point as a unit concentrated load moves across the structure.

key_concepts.explanation: The absolute governing principle for drawing ILDs. It states that the ILD for any stress function (reaction, shear, moment) in a structure is directly proportional to the deflected shape of the structure obtained by removing the restraint corresponding to that function and introducing a unit displacement in its direction.

To find the maximum bending moment under a specific wheel load in a train of moving loads, position the load train such that the resultant of all loads and the specific wheel load are equidistant from the center of the beam span.

sections.title: Matrix Methods of Structural Analysis
sections.description: Advanced computational methods used to solve highly indeterminate structures using matrix algebra.

key_concepts.explanation: The primary unknowns are joint displacements. Kinematic indeterminacy dictates the size of the stiffness matrix [K]. It is the preferred method for computer applications because the formulation is straightforward even for highly redundant structures.
The primary unknowns are redundant forces. Static indeterminacy dictates the size of the flexibility matrix [F]. The flexibility matrix is the inverse of the stiffness matrix ([F] = [K]^-1).
